text:
maria: quick FYI, hitting a weird thing with our Go client + http2 — cancelling the request context during a streaming response sometimes leaves goroutines open and connections stuck in CLOSE_WAIT. not 100% repro yet.

sam: can you paste a minimal repro or the client config you use?

maria: basic setup:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  DisableKeepAlives: false,
  ForceAttemptHTTP2: true,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 0} // streaming responses
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
// we cancel ctx while reading from resp.Body
```
I'm calling cancel() from another goroutine when we hit a global timeout. sometimes the goroutine reading resp.Body never returns.

kai: two quick checks: are you always closing resp.Body? If you cancel while a Read is blocked, Close() should unblock it, but if you neither Close nor fully drain the body that can hang reuse. Also try tr.CloseIdleConnections() in repro to see if it frees things.

nora: streaming quirk: if you stop reading mid-stream and want the connection reusable, you need to drain the body (io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)) before Close(). otherwise the connection is trashed. If you don't care about reuse, set req.Header.Set("Connection", "close") or transport.DisableKeepAlives = true (more costly).

sam: also check per-attempt context handling for retries — if your retry loop does: for { req = req.WithContext(ctx); client.Do(req) } and ctx is the same outer context, Cancel might cancel all attempts properly, but you can leak cancel funcs if you do WithTimeout/WithCancel inside the loop and forget to call cancel. remember to call cancel() after each attempt.

maria: good point — our retry wrapper creates a child ctx per attempt but I forgot to defer cancel inside the loop, so that would leak timers. will fix.

kai: tunables that helped us: lower MaxIdleConnsPerHost to something closer to concurrency (avoid huge idle queue), set ResponseHeaderTimeout to catch stuck handshakes, and keep IdleConnTimeout reasonably low in environments with lots of short-lived streams. also ResponseHeaderTimeout ensures RoundTrip returns faster on bad peers.

nora: for http2 specifically, the Go stdlib's auto http2 stack can hide stream-level details. if you're cancelling and still seeing stuck streams, try enabling runtime debug: `GODEBUG=http2debug=1` to watch stream states.

maria: streaming + retries interaction Q: when an attempt fails halfway through, we retry with exponential backoff. Any tips to ensure we don't leak socket states across attempts?

sam: always Close resp.Body on error path. If you have a wrapper that returns the body to caller, ensure the caller gets ownership and closes. For retries inside the client, close before next attempt. Also consider a small per-attempt deadline: `attemptCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, attemptTimeout)` so long stuck reads don't block the whole flow.

kai: one more: if you hit a pathological peer that ignores RST, you might need to use transport.ConnPool tuning or drop the connection by closing IdleConns. For heavy streaming, consider a dedicated transport per worker with smaller pools.

maria: awesome. I'll: 1) fix missing cancel defers, 2) ensure Close/Drain on all paths, 3) add per-attempt timeouts, 4) lower MaxIdleConnsPerHost in staging and run the repro.

deploy-bot: note: runtime v1.12.2 released — includes http transport metrics + `transport.fail_on_unread_response` flag (opt-in) that can help catch unread-body issues. rolling to staging now. :rocket:

maria: thanks — will try with that runtime and report back. :thumbsup:
